```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,fig.width=9,fig.height=5,dpi=120)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
source("R/genesis.R")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size=12))
root <- "data/processed/genesis"
if(file.exists(file.path(root,"PREPARING"))) stop("Genesis data preparation is in progress; finish scripts/prepare_genesis.R before rendering")
needed <- c("tracks.csv.gz","sites.csv.gz","static_covariates.csv.gz",
            "landcover_fractions.csv.gz","landcover_manifest.csv","input_manifest.csv","design.json")
if(!all(file.exists(file.path(root,needed)))) {
  stop("Prepare real inputs first: Rscript scripts/prepare_genesis.R")
}
config <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(root,"design.json"),simplifyVector=TRUE)
stopifnot(params$radius_m %in% config$radii_m, params$bootstrap>=199,
          params$min_coverage>0, params$min_coverage<=1)
prepared_manifest <- readr::read_csv(file.path(root,"landcover_manifest.csv"),show_col_types=FALSE)
if(!"design_sha256" %in% names(prepared_manifest) ||
   !all(prepared_manifest$design_sha256==config$design_sha256) ||
   !setequal(prepared_manifest$landcover_year,config$years-1L)) {
  stop("Land-cover manifest does not match the sampled design; rerun preparation")
}
out <- "outputs/genesis"
dir.create(out,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
set.seed(params$seed)
```

# Question and design

The hypothesis is that **reported tornado genesis occurs preferentially over
landscapes with lower aerodynamic roughness, conditional on the measured
covariates and the matched comparison design**. A separate hypothesis is that
roughness influences formation differently from persistence. We test two
associations, without assuming that tornado ends are unaffected by roughness:

1. **Paired endpoints:** is a tornado's reported start smoother than its own end?
2. **Matched local background:** is a reported start smoother than nearby available
   locations, after adjustment for elevation, elevation variability, and population?

The study retains the original domain, **102–95°W and 36–42°N**, and uses SPC
whole-track records from **2000–2024**. Eligibility is based on a valid start
inside this domain. Actual ends outside the domain are retained, with additional
land-cover coverage around them; endpoints are never created by clipping a track.
An additional comparison restricts both ends to the domain to examine boundary
selection. Neither analysis uses tornado-width buffers or cell-intersection counts.

The [SPC actual-tornado archive](https://www.spc.noaa.gov/wcm/) is a curated
whole-track source, not independent physical verification of every reported
endpoint. We use `sg = 1` records, remove exact duplicate rows, and retain source
row identifiers because `om` is not always unique. All intensity ratings are
included. Maximum EF rating and final path length are not adjustment covariates:
they could be consequences of the process being studied.

# Whole tracks and endpoint quality

```{r input}
tracks <- readr::read_csv(file.path(root,"tracks.csv.gz"),show_col_types=FALSE)
sites <- readr::read_csv(file.path(root,"sites.csv.gz"),show_col_types=FALSE)
static <- readr::read_csv(file.path(root,"static_covariates.csv.gz"),show_col_types=FALSE)
fractions <- readr::read_csv(file.path(root,"landcover_fractions.csv.gz"),show_col_types=FALSE)
lookup <- readr::read_csv("data/metadata/aersurface_roughness.csv",show_col_types=FALSE)
stopifnot(all(tracks$yr %in% 2000:2024),all(sites$landcover_year==sites$year-1),
          !anyDuplicated(tracks$track_id),!anyDuplicated(sites$site_id),
          all(sites$track_id %in% tracks$track_id))

quality <- data.frame(
  quantity=c("Eligible starts", "Invalid or missing ends", "Identical valid endpoints",
             "Distinct valid endpoint pairs", "Distinct pairs with end outside domain"),
  records=c(nrow(tracks),sum(!tracks$valid_end),
            sum(tracks$valid_end & !tracks$distinct_end),sum(tracks$distinct_end),
            sum(tracks$distinct_end & !tracks$end_in_domain)))
knitr::kable(quality)
references <- sites[sites$role=="background",]
origins <- sites[sites$role=="start",]
origins <- origins[match(references$track_id,origins$track_id),]
xy_start <- st_coordinates(st_transform(st_as_sf(origins,coords=c("lon","lat"),crs=4326),genesis_crs))
xy_reference <- st_coordinates(st_transform(st_as_sf(references,coords=c("lon","lat"),crs=4326),genesis_crs))
reference_distance_km <- sqrt(rowSums((xy_reference-xy_start)^2))/1000
stopifnot(all(reference_distance_km>=config$inner_km-1e-6),
          all(reference_distance_km<=config$outer_km+1e-6),
          all(references$lon>=-102 & references$lon<=-95 & references$lat>=36 & references$lat<=42))
knitr::kable(data.frame(reference_points=nrow(references),
  minimum_distance_km=min(reference_distance_km),maximum_distance_km=max(reference_distance_km)),digits=3)
annual <- as.data.frame(table(tracks$yr))
names(annual) <- c("year","starts")
ggplot(annual,aes(year,starts))+geom_col(fill="steelblue")+
  labs(x=NULL,y="Reported whole-track starts")+theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=60,hjust=1))
```

Invalid ends are not imputed. Identical-coordinate tracks remain eligible for
local-background modeling but cannot supply distinct paired endpoints. Coordinate
rounding is especially relevant to short tracks and the 500 m scale. The report
therefore includes a sensitivity analysis requiring at least 1 km endpoint
separation; that restriction can itself select for persistence, so it is not the
primary analysis.

```{r map, fig.cap="Eligible starts in the original study domain."}
starts_sf <- st_as_sf(tracks,coords=c("slon","slat"),crs=4326)
states <- st_as_sf(maps::map("state",fill=TRUE,plot=FALSE))
ggplot()+geom_sf(data=states,fill="gray97",color="gray60",linewidth=.3)+
  geom_sf(data=starts_sf,color="steelblue",size=.5,alpha=.5)+
  coord_sf(xlim=c(-102,-95),ylim=c(36,42),expand=FALSE)+labs(x=NULL,y=NULL)
```

# Pre-event aerodynamic roughness proxy

Each event in year *y* uses **Annual NLCD land cover from year y − 1**, from
Collection 1 Version 1 (1999–2023). This avoids assigning post-event forest loss
to the tornado's pre-event landscape. Annual classification remains imperfect,
and prior-year cover can miss land-use changes before the storm. The preparation
script uses a bundled official discovery response from the
[USGS Water STAC catalog](https://api.water.usgs.gov/gdp/pygeoapi/stac/stac-collection/nlcd/nlcd-LndCov?f=html),
substitutes the year in the versioned annual filename, and caches native 30 m regional crops. It records source URLs, metadata and crop
checksums, years, and resolution in the land-cover manifest.

We assign seasonal aerodynamic roughness lengths to the 16 land-cover classes
using non-airport, non-arid values from **EPA AERSURFACE Table 6-6**. The calendar
proxy uses season 1 for November–February (no persistent snow assumed), season 3
for March–May, season 4 for June–August, and season 5 for September–October.
Actual snow cover, crop height, harvest dates, and airport footprints are not
observed. These choices are approximations, not a complete AERSURFACE run.
[Source and seasonal definitions](https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=P101DBVE.txt).

Within each circular neighborhood, native pixel-center class fractions define an
**isotropic geometric-mean roughness index**:

\[
\log_2 z_{0,\mathrm{index}}=\sum_c f_c\log_2 z_{0,c}.
\]

This is an explicit land-cover proxy, not a measurement of effective drag or a
wind-direction-weighted inflow exposure. Equal-area projected pixels receive
equal weights; the neighborhood boundary is approximated by pixel centers.
We also fit a constant midsummer lookup sensitivity to assess the calendar
assignment. Open water remains part of the available landscape; a low-water
neighborhood sensitivity is included.

```{r covariates}
knitr::kable(lookup,digits=3,caption="EPA seasonal class roughness lengths in metres.")
get_covariates <- function(radius) {
  f <- fractions[fractions$radius_m==radius,]
  if(nrow(f)!=nrow(sites)||anyDuplicated(f$site_id)) stop("Incomplete or duplicated land-cover cache")
  x <- add_roughness(sites,f,lookup,params$min_coverage)
  x <- merge(x,static,by="site_id",sort=FALSE)
  if(nrow(x)!=nrow(sites)) stop("Incomplete static covariate cache")
  x
}
x <- get_covariates(params$radius_m)
knitr::kable(data.frame(quantity=c("Neighborhood radius (m)","Sampled reference points per start",
    "Reference inner radius (km)","Reference outer radius (km)","Sites with insufficient land-cover coverage"),
  value=c(params$radius_m,config$n_controls,config$inner_km,config$outer_km,sum(!x$landcover_ok))))
```

Elevation mean and neighborhood elevation SD come from the original 15-arc-second
Viewfinder Panoramas DEM, evaluated over a fixed 1 km radius. These control for
**topographic** variation separately from land-cover roughness. Interpolated GPW
v3 **year-2000** density is a coarse, static reporting proxy. It does not account
for all reporting differences, contemporary population, roads, visibility, or
changes in damage indicators. Missing or invalid covariates exclude the whole
matched set, not individual alternatives chosen selectively.

# Paired endpoint comparison

For each complete distinct pair, compute the start-minus-end difference in
log2 roughness. Negative values mean the start is smoother. Bootstrap intervals
resample **calendar days**, carrying all pairs from a sampled day together.
Days are a proxy for shared storm/outbreak conditions, not validated storm IDs.

```{r paired}
paired <- complete_matched_sets(x,"endpoints",tracks=tracks)
paired_stats <- paired_difference(paired,bootstrap=params$bootstrap,seed=params$seed)
knitr::kable(paired_stats$summary,digits=3)
ggplot(paired_stats$pairs,aes(difference))+geom_histogram(binwidth=.25,fill="steelblue",color="white")+
  geom_vline(xintercept=0,linetype=2)+labs(x="Start minus end log2 roughness",y="Tornado pairs")
```

The conditional logistic model uses one start and one end per tornado, with a
stratum for each track. A negative roughness coefficient indicates that a rougher
location is less likely to be the start within its pair. This is **endpoint
asymmetry among reported tornadoes**, not an absolute genesis probability or a
causal estimate. Storm motion through geographic gradients, changing environments,
and roughness-dependent termination can also create asymmetry.

```{r paired-model}
paired_unadjusted <- fit_genesis_clogit(paired,adjusted=FALSE)
paired_adjusted <- fit_genesis_clogit(paired)
summary(paired_adjusted)
```

# Matched local-background genesis model

This rerun uses a 5–30 km reference annulus. Reference points are now checked
against the exact longitude/latitude bounds. The earlier four-corner projected
polygon admitted 51 points slightly north of 42°N in the 2–10 km run. Differences
from that published run therefore include both the annulus change and this correction.
The wider annulus increases landscape contrast and also allows larger meteorological
and reporting gradients between a start and its reference locations.

Each start is matched to **ten** locations sampled uniformly by area within a
**`r config$inner_km`–`r config$outer_km` km annulus**, restricted to the original domain. Boundary annuli are
truncated by that domain, rather than wrapping or shifting. The random seed and
all sampled coordinates are saved. These are reference locations, not confirmed
non-tornadic storms, and a reference location may have experienced a tornado on
another occasion. Whole tracks with missing or identical ends remain eligible.

The response is the observed start (one case) versus its ten alternatives. Track
strata hold shared event date, season, and broad local context fixed. The adjusted
model includes log2 roughness, elevation mean, elevation SD, and log2(population + 1).
All fitted models use Efron's conditional likelihood with one case per set, which
agrees with the exact conditional likelihood here and permits robust sandwich
covariance clustered by calendar day.

```{r genesis-model}
genesis <- complete_matched_sets(x,"genesis",n_controls=config$n_controls)
genesis_unadjusted <- fit_genesis_clogit(genesis,adjusted=FALSE)
genesis_adjusted <- fit_genesis_clogit(genesis)
summary(genesis_adjusted)
```

```{r main-results}
result <- function(model,design,adjustment,term="log2_z0") {
  cbind(design=design,adjustment=adjustment,clogit_effect(model,term))
}
results <- rbind(result(paired_unadjusted,"Paired endpoints","Unadjusted"),
                 result(paired_adjusted,"Paired endpoints","Adjusted"),
                 result(genesis_unadjusted,"Local background","Unadjusted"),
                 result(genesis_adjusted,"Local background","Adjusted"))
knitr::kable(results,digits=3,caption="Odds ratios per doubling of neighborhood roughness, with date-clustered 95% intervals.")
usage <- data.frame(design=c("Paired endpoints","Local background"),
                    matched_sets=c(length(unique(paired$track_id)),length(unique(genesis$track_id))),
                    days=c(length(unique(paired$event_date)),length(unique(genesis$event_date))))
knitr::kable(usage)
plot_results <- results
plot_results$label <- paste(plot_results$design,tolower(plot_results$adjustment),sep=", ")
plot_results$label <- factor(plot_results$label,levels=rev(plot_results$label))
ggplot(plot_results,aes(odds_ratio,label,xmin=lower_95,xmax=upper_95))+
  geom_pointrange()+geom_vline(xintercept=1,linetype=2)+scale_x_log10()+
  labs(x="Odds ratio per doubling of roughness (95% interval)",y=NULL)
```

The adjusted local-background estimate is **`r round(clogit_effect(genesis_adjusted)$odds_ratio,3)`**
(95% interval **`r round(clogit_effect(genesis_adjusted)$lower_95,3)`–`r round(clogit_effect(genesis_adjusted)$upper_95,3)`**)
per doubling of the roughness index. The adjusted paired-endpoint estimate is
**`r round(clogit_effect(paired_adjusted)$odds_ratio,3)`**
(**`r round(clogit_effect(paired_adjusted)$lower_95,3)`–`r round(clogit_effect(paired_adjusted)$upper_95,3)`**).
These two coefficients address different comparisons; their difference is not a
formal test of genesis versus persistence.

For the local-background model, an odds ratio below one indicates lower relative
odds that a location is the reported start as roughness increases, within these
sampled alternatives. The model does not estimate the chance that an arbitrary
storm produces a tornado. Meteorological opportunity is unmeasured: nearby
background locations were not necessarily traversed by the parent storm.
Population adjustment and local matching do not establish “all else equal.”

# Reference-annulus comparison

The earlier 2–10 km estimates are preserved from commit `bc03c95`. Its sampler
admitted 51 background points north of the intended boundary. The comparison below
therefore includes both the annulus change and the boundary correction; it does
not isolate a distance effect. It is shown only at the original 1 km exposure scale.

```{r annulus-comparison, results='asis'}
if(params$radius_m==1000) {
  baseline <- readr::read_csv("data/metadata/genesis_reference_2_10_baseline.csv",show_col_types=FALSE)
  old <- baseline[baseline$design=="Local background",]
  new <- results[results$design=="Local background",]
  comparison <- rbind(
    data.frame(annulus="2–10 km (earlier boundary)",old[c("adjustment","odds_ratio","lower_95","upper_95")]),
    data.frame(annulus=paste0(config$inner_km,"–",config$outer_km," km (exact bounds)"),
               new[c("adjustment","odds_ratio","lower_95","upper_95")]))
  cat(knitr::kable(comparison,format="html",digits=3),sep="\n")
  readr::write_csv(comparison,file.path(out,"reference_annulus_comparison.csv"))
}
```

# Sensitivity and identification checks

The neighborhood-scale fits below share the sampled sites and fixed 1 km terrain
adjustments. The paired ≥1 km fit addresses very short or rounded tracks; the
both-ends-inside fit examines boundary selection. The midsummer-only lookup
removes seasonal class-value assignment. The low-water fit restricts complete
matched sets to neighborhoods with less than 5% water at every alternative;
this changes the geographic sample and is not a general correction for water.

A developed-cover adjustment adds neighborhood developed fraction as another
reporting/damage-indicator proxy. Because developed cover also contributes to
roughness, this changes the conditional contrast. A separate genesis fit requires
starts at least `r config$outer_km` km from the domain boundary, so reference annuli are untruncated.

```{r sensitivity}
sensitivity <- list()
for(radius in config$radii_m) {
  xx <- get_covariates(radius)
  for(design in c("endpoints","genesis")) {
    dd <- complete_matched_sets(xx,design,n_controls=config$n_controls,tracks=tracks)
    sensitivity[[paste(radius,design)]] <- cbind(test=paste0(radius," m"),design=design,
      sets=length(unique(dd$track_id)),clogit_effect(fit_genesis_clogit(dd)))
  }
}
for(test in c("Endpoints at least 1 km apart","Both ends inside domain","Midsummer lookup","Low-water neighborhoods")) {
  for(design in if(test %in% c("Endpoints at least 1 km apart","Both ends inside domain")) "endpoints" else c("endpoints","genesis")) {
    xx <- x
    if(test=="Low-water neighborhoods") xx$landcover_ok <- xx$landcover_ok & xx$water_fraction<.05
    dd <- complete_matched_sets(xx,design,n_controls=config$n_controls,tracks=tracks,
      min_displacement_km=if(test=="Endpoints at least 1 km apart") 1 else 0,
      ends_inside=test=="Both ends inside domain")
    term <- if(test=="Midsummer lookup") "log2_z0_summer" else "log2_z0"
    sensitivity[[paste(test,design)]] <- cbind(test=test,design=design,
      sets=length(unique(dd$track_id)),clogit_effect(fit_genesis_clogit(dd,roughness=term),term))
  }
}
for(design in c("endpoints","genesis")) {
  dd <- if(design=="endpoints") paired else genesis
  sensitivity[[paste("Developed-cover adjustment",design)]] <- cbind(
    test="Developed-cover adjustment",design=design,sets=length(unique(dd$track_id)),
    clogit_effect(fit_genesis_clogit(dd,developed_adjustment=TRUE)))
}
start_geometry <- st_transform(st_as_sf(tracks,coords=c("slon","slat"),crs=4326),genesis_crs)
edge_distance <- as.numeric(st_distance(start_geometry,
  st_boundary(st_transform(genesis_domain(),genesis_crs))))/1000
interior <- genesis[genesis$track_id %in% tracks$track_id[edge_distance>=config$outer_km],]
sensitivity[["Untruncated reference annuli"]] <- cbind(test="Untruncated reference annuli",
  design="genesis",sets=length(unique(interior$track_id)),clogit_effect(fit_genesis_clogit(interior)))
sensitivity <- dplyr::bind_rows(sensitivity)
knitr::kable(sensitivity,digits=3)
```

We examine the amount of within-set roughness variation: pairs with equal
roughness provide no direct contrast for its coefficient. Confidence intervals
are model-based, clustered by date, and do not propagate land-cover mapping,
lookup-value, or coordinate uncertainty. Date clustering also leaves possible
spatial dependence between events on different days unaddressed. Sensitivity fits are exploratory and
are not multiple independent confirmations.

```{r variation}
variation <- function(d) {
  span <- vapply(split(d$log2_z0,d$track_id),function(z) diff(range(z)),numeric(1))
  data.frame(sets=length(span),zero_roughness_span=sum(span<1e-10),
             median_log2_span=median(span))
}
knitr::kable(rbind(cbind(design="Endpoints",variation(paired)),
                   cbind(design="Local background",variation(genesis))),digits=3)
```

# Interpretation and next steps

For the primary adjusted local-background model, the 95% interval
**`r if(clogit_effect(genesis_adjusted)$upper_95<1) "lies below one" else if(clogit_effect(genesis_adjusted)$lower_95>1) "lies above one" else "includes one"`**.
For the paired model, it
**`r if(clogit_effect(paired_adjusted)$upper_95<1) "lies below one" else if(clogit_effect(paired_adjusted)$lower_95>1) "lies above one" else "includes one"`**.
An interval below one supports a negative association under that specification;
an interval including one leaves the direction uncertain. These comparisons do
not establish the presence or absence of a physical effect.

The developed-cover sensitivity gives a local-background odds ratio of
**`r round(sensitivity$odds_ratio[sensitivity$test=="Developed-cover adjustment" & sensitivity$design=="genesis"],3)`**
(95% interval
**`r round(sensitivity$lower_95[sensitivity$test=="Developed-cover adjustment" & sensitivity$design=="genesis"],3)`–`r round(sensitivity$upper_95[sensitivity$test=="Developed-cover adjustment" & sensitivity$design=="genesis"],3)`**).
This demonstrates sensitivity to the reporting-proxy specification. Developed
cover also contributes to the exposure itself, so the additional adjustment
changes the contrast being estimated. The endpoint result is also sensitive to
seasonal lookup values and the low-water sample restriction. These exploratory
results motivate better roughness and reporting measurements; they do not select
a uniquely preferred physical explanation.


The two comparisons address different questions. A smoother start than end could
reflect preferential genesis, preferential termination over rough terrain, or
storm motion across a roughness gradient. A smoother start than local background
is more directly relevant to genesis location, but remains conditional on
reporting and an approximate landscape availability definition. Neither design
proves a physical effect or verifies the premise that persistence is unaffected.

A stronger subsequent study would define available locations using radar-tracked
parent storms, including non-tornadic storms, and test termination with detailed
surveyed paths. Additional priorities are measured inflow direction, season-specific
vegetation height, updated population/accessibility covariates, coordinate-jitter
sensitivity, and alternative reference-distance/sampling seeds. Those checks are
not claimed to have been completed here.

Related endpoint designs include [Muncy (2021)](http://rave.ohiolink.edu/etdc/view?acc_num=ohiou1628513174226383)
and [Dison (2026)](https://scholarsjunction.msstate.edu/td/6885/).
The role of friction can be more complex than uniform suppression of genesis;
see [Roberts and Xue (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1175/JAS-D-16-0364.1).
